# RustyNES v2.6.11 "Exposure"

A picture is a gate the ladder did not have.

All 141 co-simulation gates THEN IN THE SUITE were green (it ends this release at 142, the one it added) and two of six commercial games rendered wrong.

**The emulation core is unchanged.** No chip crate changes, so AccuracyCoin 141/141 (RAM decoder) and nestest 0-diff hold by construction. The work is in the sibling's RTL, in the montage that found it, and in two release-documentation gates.

## The gate

| # | criterion | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the six commercial titles render identically | **all six byte-identical** to the oracle over 61,440 pixels each |
| 2 | the fix is not a compensation | a **control**: the pre-M10K-fix RTL differs by the **identical** 16,565 pixels |
| 3 | the read and fetch paths are unchanged | AccuracyCoin identical entry for entry across all 146 entries |
| 4 | no regression | **142 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** — 141 before this release's new gate |
| 5 | the release-lead gates fail on the real defect | both mutated and CAUGHT; the chain gate then caught the bump script itself |

## A CHR-RAM write was taking the address built for fetches

`rtl/ppu2c02.sv` presents one address to the cartridge:

```systemverilog
assign chr_addr = ((dot[0] == 1'b0) || (pd_stage == 3'd4))
                    ? {chr_addr_raw[13:8], octal_latch}
                    : chr_addr_raw;
```

That composite is correct and **load-bearing**. It models the 2C02's shared address/data pins — the low byte held in the octal latch across the read dot — and AccuracyCoin's `ALE + Read` and `Hybrid Addresses` both depend on it. Removing it fails those entries.

It is the wrong address for a **write**. A `$2007` write must land at `v`, and the octal latch is not `v`: it loads from the fetch cadence while rendering and from the PPU DATA machine's ALE stage otherwise, so a CHR-RAM write during rendering lands wherever the current fetch happens to point. The result is **correct layout with scrambled tiles**, which is why it survived — nothing about the frame looks structurally broken.

The fix separates the two paths rather than changing either.

| board | game | CHR | wrong pixels |
|---|---|---|---:|
| NROM | 1942 | 8 KiB ROM | 0 |
| MMC1 | Adventures of Lolo | 32 KiB ROM | 0 |
| CNROM | Arkanoid | 16 KiB ROM | 0 |
| MMC3 | Bad Dudes | 128 KiB ROM | 0 |
| UxROM | 1943: The Battle of Midway | **RAM** | **16,565 → 0** |
| AxROM | Battletoads & Double Dragon | **RAM** | **1,702 → 0** |

The split is exactly CHR-ROM against CHR-RAM, which named the mechanism before any tracing.

**A control says it is not v2.6.10's regression.** That release folded `chr` to a single write port for M10K inference and touched the same signal, so it was the obvious suspect. It is not: the pre-M10K-fix RTL differs from the oracle by the **identical 16,565 pixels**. The defect dates from the cartridge landing in v2.6.9.

## Reached 9,600 times, compared never

Not because the path is unreached — the DUT asserts `chr_wr` **9,600 times** in the Battletoads run alone. The reason is what the gates *compare*:

- **Three gates out of 141 compare a framebuffer** — `bg-render`, `sprite-render`, `sprite-mask`. All three ship **CHR-ROM**, so `chr_wr` never fires in the only gates that would render the consequence.
- **Every other gate is CPU-side.** The bus gate compares `pc`, `bus_addr`, `bus_data` and `bus_access`; the checkpoint streams hash nine `Observable` fields, all CPU-side.
- **AccuracyCoin is CHR-ROM**, so the 146-entry status vector — the widest gate in the suite — never asserts `chr_wr` at all.
- The rung-7 gates' own comment says what they are for: *"these gates are about BANKING and nothing else."* It was accurate, and it was the whole coverage.

The suite reads 141 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped **both before and after** the fix.

## The montage

`RustyNES_MiSTer/screenshots/montage.png`, six commercial titles rendered by the RTL under Verilator, one per supported board, referenced from a new "What it renders" section that states what the picture is **not**: not hardware, one frame each, and the palette applied *afterwards*, because what the RTL emits and what every gate compares is the pre-palette `index_framebuffer`.

`tb/make_montage.sh` takes `--verify` and **refuses to publish a tile that differs from the oracle**, and fails closed on a missing capture rather than producing a five-tile montage that still looks finished.

Frames are joined to the DUT by the manifest's **CPU-cycle count**, not the frame number: the DUT counts cycles, the exporter counts frames, and the first `run_frame()` after power-on advances zero cycles, so the two do not convert by multiplication.

## Bus conflicts: the oracle modelled them and the DUT did not

`rtl/cart/cart.sv` said bus conflicts were not modelled, named it as a decision, and ended with the right instruction: *"If a golden ever disagrees on a write to a mapped address, this is the first thing to suspect."*

No golden ever disagreed, and the reason is in the harness rather than the console. `mkmapper.py`'s `_rom` writes **`$FF` at the select address**, with a comment saying why — *"so a bus conflict (modelled or not) is the identity on the written byte."* Every mapper gate is immune to the behaviour **by construction**, and the rung-7 loop says so in its own words: *"these gates are about BANKING and nothing else."*

**The rule is the wiki's**, stated outright on `Bus_conflict.xhtml`: the CPU and the mask ROMs both *"drive a 0 more strongly than a 1"*, which *"implies that an emulator should use the bitwise AND of the value from the CPU and the value from the ROM"*.

**What is a measurement rather than a reading is which board.** The oracle's `m003_cnrom.rs` ANDs with the PRG byte, so the two consoles disagreed on **every mapper-3 write whose value differs from the ROM byte** — and nothing could see it.

`mapper3cnrombusconflict066` writes to addresses holding `$01` and `$00` instead, with two `$FF` controls so a broken register stays distinguishable from a missing conflict:

| slot | write | ROM byte | oracle | DUT before | DUT after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 control | `$03` → `$DFFF` | `$FF` | `$03` | `$03` | `$03` |
| 1 | `$03` → `$D100` | `$01` | `$01` | **`$03`** | `$01` |
| 2 | `$03` → `$9000` | `$00` | `$00` | **`$03`** | `$00` |
| 3 control | `$02` → `$DFFF` | `$FF` | `$02` | `$02` | `$02` |

Slot 2 is not redundant with slot 1: it separates "ANDs with the ROM byte" from "ANDs with something". After the fix the entire 2 KiB of work RAM is identical and **146 nine-field checkpoints** match. `mapper3cnrom061` is unaffected in both directions, which makes this a strict addition. Two mutations CAUGHT — dropping the AND, and ANDing with a constant that satisfies slot 1 alone.

**UxROM, AxROM and NROM stay unmodelled**, for the same reason rather than a different one: the oracle does not model them either, so modelling them here would **create** a divergence rather than close one. That leaves a shared inaccuracy against hardware on mapper 2, named in `docs/rung7-mappers.md` rather than fixed on one side. The old comment justified the omission with the wiki's *"the relevant games all work around this in software"* — which the wiki says about **mapper 2**, and not about mapper 3, where it was being applied.

## Eight release leads described v2.6.10 as v2.6.9

The v2.6.10 bump moved the version token and left the summary prose after it, so every lead read `v2.6.10 "Inference" — <v2.6.9's summary> ... Built on **v2.6.8**`. Two wrong claims from one edit: v2.6.10 described as the previous release's work, and **v2.6.9 gone from the lineage entirely**. `docs/STATUS.md` was worst — it named **v2.6.10 with the codename "Abeyance"**.

Every existing check passed, and each did so **correctly**: they pin the version token, and the token was right.

Prose cannot be audited. An ordering can, so two gates are added and both are demonstrated to fail:

- `a_release_line_chain_does_not_skip_a_release` — the first release a chain names after the current one must be the release immediately before it in the CHANGELOG, **derived** rather than written down. It walks *every* chain in a file, and accepts both link spellings this corpus uses.
- `a_codename_near_the_current_version_is_the_changelog_codename` — a codename quoted within 40 characters of the current version, past a date or a dash. A second check rather than a loosening of the first.

Three findings from building them, each recorded because each cost something:

- **The hand-written document list was wrong on its first use.** It named six documents; the drift reached **eight**, and `SUPPORT.md` and `SECURITY.md` were not on it. The list is now derived from the `ANCHORS` table — a hand list silently omits exactly as a glob silently widens.
- **The second gate's own first run found a false positive**, before it shipped: `README.md`'s version badge puts the version inside an HTML attribute, where the nearest quote is a delimiter and the "codename" it yields is a space followed by `alt=`. The narrower rule tried first — reject a gap containing `=<>/` — did **not** catch it, because the offending gap is `-blue.svg`. A version-to-codename gap never contains a **letter**.
- **The chain gate caught `bump_release.py` itself.** Run for this release, the script left two documents un-demoted and two chains still headed at v2.6.9. The gate named all four on its first real use — two of which turned out to be the gate's own marker being too narrow for the script's second link spelling, which is how that widening got measured rather than guessed.

## Also

`crates/rustynes-cosim/Cargo.lock` still recorded 2.6.9. The crate is excluded from the workspace, so `cargo build --workspace` never refreshes it — the same class of defect as the leads above.

## Not closed

**The v2.6.10 bitstream carries this defect.** A published version is immutable here, so it cannot be back-fitted; `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.6.11.rbf` is built from the corrected RTL.

**Rung 6.** No DE10-Nano and no SuperStation One are attached to this machine — confirmed by checking the USB bus, serial devices, removable block devices and mounts, not assumed. No hardware has run the bitstream.

**Bus conflicts on UxROM, AxROM and NROM** remain unmodelled — CNROM's are modelled from this release. The other three stay unmodelled because the oracle does not model them either, so modelling them in the DUT would *create* a divergence rather than close one. That leaves a shared inaccuracy against hardware on mapper 2, named rather than fixed on one side.
